en.headline: CUHK study links PMOS in mothers to higher risks in children
en.dek: Daughters of women with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome had 3.6 times the rate of menstrual disorders, researchers said.
body: A Chinese University of Hong Kong medical school study found that polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, or PMOS, formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome, was associated with higher endocrine and metabolic risks in patients’ children as well as in the patients themselves.

Researchers compared 71 mothers with PMOS and their children aged 15 to 25 with 506 mothers without the condition and their children, using data collected between 2020 and 2024. They said 58.3 per cent of daughters of PMOS patients had menstrual irregularities, 3.6 times the comparison group, and that more than 10 per cent of those daughters were themselves diagnosed with PMOS. Sons of patients had nearly three times the risk of hypertension and metabolic syndrome.

Dr Jacqueline Chung Pui-wah, chairperson of CUHK’s Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, said the cause of PMOS remains unclear but may be related to insulin resistance. She said some patients improve with weight loss and that surgery can restore ovulation in a majority of selected cases.

Lead researcher Noel Ng Yat-hei said the findings suggested early reproductive and cardiometabolic changes can already appear as the children enter adulthood. The team advised people with a family history of the condition to monitor their health earlier.

zh.headline: 中大研究：PMOS患者子女內分泌代謝風險較高
zh.dek: 中大醫學院研究指，多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症患者的女兒月經失調比率達對照組3.6倍，兒子高血壓及代謝綜合症風險亦較高。
body: 香港中文大學醫學院一項研究發現，多內分泌代謝性卵巢綜合症（PMOS，前稱多囊卵巢綜合症）不單影響患者本身，亦與子女較高的內分泌及代謝風險有關。
研究於2020至2024年進行，比較71名患有PMOS的母親及其15至25歲子女，與506名沒有該病的母親及其子女。團隊指，患者女兒有58.3%出現月經不調，為對照組的3.6倍；逾一成患者女兒同樣確診PMOS。患者兒子出現高血壓及代謝綜合症的風險則接近對照組的三倍。
中大醫學院婦產科學系系主任鍾佩榜表示，PMOS成因仍未完全清楚，相信或與胰島素抗阻有關。她指部分患者可透過減重改善情況，亦有個案可經手術恢復排卵。
首席研究員吳逸暎表示，研究顯示患者子女踏入成年期已可出現生殖及心血管代謝的早期變化。團隊建議有家族病史的人士及早監察健康狀況。
